strengths: The scalar-bijection contribution is technically interesting: the cubic-rational, sinh-conjugation, and cubic-conjugation families have explicit parameter constraints, tractable Jacobians, and closed-form inverses. The appendix derives the cubic-rational monotonicity range (-1 < lambda < 8) and the radial Jacobian.

The evaluation is unusually broad, covering controlled 1D and 2D problems, CIFAR-10, five UCI datasets, and a 400-dimensional phi-4 lattice model. Multiple seeds are reported for several central experiments, and the lattice experiments expose the important failure of model-sampled ESS to detect mode collapse.

The radial parameterization is geometrically interpretable and potentially useful for distributions with strong radial structure. The Fourier-conditioned version offers a compact way to inspect angular dependence, while the symmetry-preserving zero-mode transformation is a sensible example of incorporating scientific structure.

The manuscript is generally clear and visually polished, with useful derivations, hyperparameter tables, runtime measurements, and an honest discussion of limited high-dimensional evidence, fixed hyperparameters, and radial-flow geometric constraints. :codex-file-citation{path="/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/experiments/runs/20260921_han_gpt_all_anonymized_review/scratch/847d2ef4952f4550b095057956b0c544/work/manuscript.pdf" purpose="source"}
No material research-ethics concern is apparent; the work concerns general density-estimation methodology and a physics application.
weaknesses: The smoothness story for radial flows is technically incomplete. Enforcing only f(0)=0 makes x -> f(||x||)x/||x|| differentiable at the center under suitable first-order conditions, but does not generally make it infinitely differentiable: generic even-order terms in f produce nonsmooth terms such as ||x||x. Angle-conditioned flows can fail even to be differentiable unless the directional first derivative is constant, and the experiments intentionally leave that constraint unenforced. Thus the displayed singular center and the claimed smooth radial behavior are in tension with the paper's central positioning.

Several headline empirical claims are not supported by controlled comparisons. The CIFAR-10 table compares the proposed RealNVP+ implementation—with ActNorm, GELU, eight analytic transforms plus an affine transform—to the published 3.49 RealNVP number rather than an affine baseline in the same implementation. Calling this a matched-architecture improvement or evidence that the scalar replacement caused the gain is therefore unjustified.

The claim of comparable quality with roughly 1000-fold fewer parameters relies heavily on qualitative 2D density plots. The Gaussian-mixture comparison provides no held-out likelihood, KL, or other quantitative metric, while the spiral comparison uses architectures and learning rates with very different inductive biases. These results establish promise on radially favorable targets, but not a robust efficiency advantage over coupling flows.

The standard tabular results are mixed: pure sinh is usually comparable to, rather than better than, the reproduced spline; the hybrid adds capacity and performs worse on HEPMASS and substantially worse on MINIBOONE. Stack depth also varies by dataset after observing instability, and parameter or compute matching is not reported.

Some framing is overstated. Table 1 marks splines as non-global even though standard neural splines define bijections on all real numbers via identity or linear tails; the actual distinction is that their nonlinear action is bounded. Likewise, Abel-Ruffini does not by itself prove that quadratic denominators are the unique nontrivial rational construction with a closed-form inverse, because structured higher-degree polynomials can remain solvable.

The phi-4 ESS improvements are modest, use only three runs, and lack uncertainty for final differences or statistical tests. The statement that these results show the smoothness advantage persists at 400 dimensions is not supported by ESS, which measures sampling quality rather than higher-order smoothness. The MCMC reference and evaluation sample counts are also insufficiently documented.

Reproducibility is only partial. Architectures and optimization settings are described well, but important details such as evaluation sample counts, CIFAR dequantization and likelihood estimation, preprocessing, checkpoint selection, exact per-dataset stack counts, and MCMC ground-truth diagnostics are absent. The manuscript mentions a library and tutorial but does not provide a usable artifact link in the submitted version.

Overall, the scalar constructions and structured-flow ideas have clear merit, but the unresolved radial regularity issue and confounded evidence behind major performance claims prevent reliable acceptance in the present form. A revision should correct the smoothness claims or enforce the necessary center regularity and add matched, quantitative baselines.

strengths: Soundness: The cubic-rational monotonicity bounds and radial-flow Jacobian are derived clearly, and the proposed scalar maps do provide tractable Jacobians and closed-form mathematical inverses under the stated parameter constraints.

Significance: Smooth scalar transformations could be useful in scientific applications involving derivatives of learned log densities. The 400-dimensional lattice-field experiment suggests applicability beyond toy problems.

Originality: Extending scalar bijections with multiple-center and angle-conditioned radial transformations is an interesting, geometrically interpretable design, although it builds directly on prior radial flows and standard conjugation constructions.
Presentation: The manuscript is generally well organized and visually polished. It explains local versus global deformation, ray preservation, and reverse-KL mode collapse clearly.
Evaluation: The paper covers several settings, often reports multiple seeds on the low-dimensional experiments, includes runtime measurements, and compares against affine and spline transformations.

Limitations and ethics: The authors appropriately acknowledge the radial architecture's geometric restrictions, lack of high-dimensional radial experiments, method-specific tuning limitations, and the origin regularity condition. No material research-ethics concern is apparent.
weaknesses: Soundness: The headline global-smoothness guarantee does not describe the implemented models. Section C.3 replaces the sinh map by a different asymptotic expression at the hard threshold |x|=15; without a smooth matching construction, this piecewise implementation is generally not C-infinity and may not even match exactly at the boundary. No continuity, invertibility, or approximation-error analysis is supplied.

Soundness: The angle-dependent radial experiments explicitly do not enforce the direction-independent derivative required for differentiability at the learned center (Section 4.2). The resulting map has an ill-defined Jacobian there, directly conflicting with repeated claims of smooth learned transformations. Calling enforcement optional or post-training does not establish the claimed property for the evaluated model.

Soundness: The claimed exceptional training stability is not demonstrated by a controlled learning-rate sweep or failure-rate comparison. Table 5 merely shows that different architectures were trained with different selected rates. Likewise, the loss-variance comparison between 42 cubic maps and three 14-knot splines is confounded by parameterization and is not replicated across seeds; attributing it to a smoother optimization landscape is unsupported.

Evaluation: The CIFAR-10 result lacks the essential matched affine control. The paper compares its altered RealNVP+ architecture—ActNorm, GELU, different prior and normalization choices, and eight analytic transforms plus an affine per layer—against the published 3.49 RealNVP number, yet attributes the 3.36–3.37 results to the scalar bijections. There is also no spline control, uncertainty, or run count.

Evaluation: Many comparisons increase depth, parameters, and computation substantially. The lattice models use eight analytic bijections plus an affine versus the stated affine and spline baselines, and the appendix reports up to 1.5–2 times spline training cost. The paper does not provide compute-matched or parameter-matched comparisons, so the modest ESS improvement from 31.85% to 39.66% cannot be isolated to the proposed functional form.

Evaluation: The strongest radial-flow evidence uses deliberately radial 2D targets. The Gaussian-mixture comparison is primarily visual, while the 1000-fold parameter claim compares very different architectures. There is no broad quantitative benchmark establishing competitiveness on non-radial targets, and radial flows are not tested beyond two dimensions.

Evaluation: Several central empirical claims are statistically weak. CIFAR-10 has no error bars; the physics result uses only three runs; the number of evaluation samples and uncertainty of ESS are omitted; and the purported smoothness benefit is demonstrated on one constructed 1D example whose second-derivative discontinuity is already inherent to finite-order splines.

Originality and significance: Conjugating a translation by an invertible monotone function is elementary, cubic inversion is classical, and compositional radial transformations extend the radial-flow construction cited from Rezende and Mohamed. The paper does not sharply distinguish its radial architecture from related conditioned or multi-center radial-flow variants, making the novelty appear incremental.

Reproducibility: Although a library is referenced and many optimizer settings are listed, decisive details remain missing: per-dataset sinh stack counts are only said to vary, run counts are not consistently reported, the bimodal lattice value of lambda is unspecified, evaluation sample counts are absent, and the numerical inverse's stability over the allowed parameter range is not validated.

Presentation: Conclusions repeatedly overstate the evidence, including 'guaranteeing smooth learned densities,' 'exceptional training stability,' and persistence of a smoothness advantage in the 400-dimensional experiment, where only ESS—not smoothness—was measured. The honest limitations discussion does not repair these unsupported central claims.

strengths: Soundness: The three scalar families have clear formulas, parameter constraints, Jacobians, and closed-form inverses; the cubic-rational monotonicity argument and radial Jacobian derivation are particularly useful.

Significance: The work evaluates the constructions beyond toy examples, including CIFAR-10, five UCI datasets, and a 400-dimensional lattice-field problem. The consistent improvement over affine coupling in the physics experiment suggests practical value.

Originality: Combining analytically invertible scalar maps with directly parameterized, optionally angle-conditioned radial flows is a coherent and fairly distinctive contribution. The zero-mode construction also illustrates useful problem-specific flow design.

Presentation: The manuscript is unusually clear and well organized, with informative visualizations, explicit discussion of local versus global deformation, and an honest account of radial flows' geometric and dimensional limitations.

Reproducibility and ethics: The appendices provide formulas, parameter transforms, target definitions, architectures, and most training hyperparameters; the cited implementation library should further help reproduction. The work poses little direct ethical risk, and no material ethical concern is apparent.
weaknesses: Soundness: The radial-flow smoothness claims are overstated. Enforcing f(0)=0 is enough for continuity, but generic radial maps x↦f(||x||)x/||x|| require stronger derivative conditions for C-infinity regularity at the center. The angle-dependent experiments do not even enforce the stated condition for differentiability there, and Figure 6 visibly contains the resulting singular point. Thus claims of guaranteed smooth learned densities do not apply uniformly to a central proposed architecture.

The empirical comparisons are often not capacity- or compute-matched. CIFAR-10 compares eight analytic bijections plus an affine map against a published affine RealNVP number rather than a same-code affine or spline baseline. Similarly, the lattice models stack eight analytic maps per layer against single affine/spline transformations. Improvements therefore cannot be attributed cleanly to the proposed functional form.

The strongest parameter-efficiency demonstrations use targets deliberately aligned with radial geometry. The spiral result compares different learning rates and architectures, while the Gaussian-mixture result is primarily visual and lacks quantitative likelihood, KL, or sampling metrics. These experiments do not establish broad superiority of radial flows.

Several conclusions exceed the evidence: the claimed smoother optimization landscape is inferred from loss variance on one 1D example; exceptional stability is largely inferred from usable learning rates under different architectures; and the claimed persistence of a smoothness advantage in 400 dimensions is not directly measured in the lattice experiment.

Statistical support is uneven. Toy studies use six seeds, but the physics comparison uses only three runs, CIFAR-10 reports no uncertainty, and the UCI table does not explain the source or number of repetitions behind its error bars. Significance testing or paired comparisons are absent.

Reproducibility remains incomplete despite the extensive appendix: the CIFAR coupling-layer counts and exact preprocessing/evaluation protocol are underspecified, exact per-dataset sinh stack counts are explicitly omitted, and runtime comparisons lack hardware and batch-size details. These omissions matter because depth is a key experimental variable.

Originality is somewhat incremental at the scalar-map level: conjugation by an invertible monotone function is a general elementary construction, and the radial architecture substantially extends an established radial-flow idea rather than introducing an entirely new paradigm. Related-work positioning could more carefully separate the genuinely novel components from these general principles.
